newsitem.title: CANADA: Noranda reopens Heath Steel zinc mine.
newsitem.headline: Noranda reopens Heath Steel zinc mine.

text.p: Noranda Inc said Wednesday it has reopened its Heath Steele zinc and lead mine in New Brunswick after an underground explosion killed one miner and injured another on Monday.
"The mine is back to normal operations and we're investigating the accident," Ivan Miller, commercial vice-president for Noranda, said in an interview.
Heath Steele produces 100,000 tonnes of zinc concentrates a year and a small amount of lead concentrates. The company lost one day's production because of the accident.
Operations in all areas of the mine have resumed except in the area where the accident occurred, the company said. The accident was in a development area and its closure will not hurt production.

The exlosion at the mine in Newcastle, New Brunswick happened in the late afternoon on Monday. It killed one 47-year-old man. A second worker is in stable condition, Noranda spokesman Gilles Gratton said.
A preliminary investigation shows that sulphur dioxide gas was released following a routine blasting operation, Gratton said.
The gas usually occurs after blasting, but workers are usually out of the way following blasts, he said.
A continuing investigation by government workplace investigators, the RCMP and the company will work to find out what went wrong.
